title: Muse: a personal agent behind Privilege

glossary.definition: Whether a persona may call a tool at all. The first gate after detection.
The business rule inside an allowed call, such as a payment limit or an export row cap.

Two PingOne Authorize rules on the airline booking tool: yours (no tickets bought by an AI agent over your limit, $500 by default) and the airline's (only premium members over $750; the tier is the PingOne user attribute airlineMemberTier, read by Authorize). Mock simulates them; Real reads the gateway's answer. The Test controls card sets the tier (Premier Gold, Premier Silver or no tier) and the agent spend limit in dollars (the PingOne attribute agentSpendLimit; an empty field means the default): in Mock it sets the simulated member and limit, in Real it writes the PingOne attributes on the demo users and reads them back.

muse.ai can book through the Airline Connector: list_flights shows the invented catalogue, and book_flight takes a destination ("Book me a flight to London tomorrow"), a price ("Book me a flight to Seattle for $450 tomorrow") or both. muse.ai's assistant asks for a destination and a day first, so include them; the connector ignores the day and needs only a price or a destination. A destination alone books the airline's own fare; a stated price is the price the rules judge, and the gateway accepts it only from this trusted connector (a real airline would price the ticket itself). The two booking rules decide: a booking within your dollar limit goes straight through to the airline server and muse.ai gets the server's answer back; over your limit it is blocked, with your limit and the fare in the message; otherwise it is held for approval. Nothing is booked unless the airline server's answer says booked true. Authorize first checks that you let this agent act for you; the connector passes on the consent you gave at sign-in, and the pre-approval for a booking within your limit, only when its owner has set up the consent bridge (and, for a limit above $500, the test controls), otherwise the booking is denied for missing consent or held.

muse.ai is a cloud assistant used as the MCP client. The Connect muse.ai card gives the connector's address (the MCP URL), the client ID, no client secret, PKCE S256, scope mcp and the redirect URI, each with a Copy button, and a prompt to paste into muse.ai so it sets the connector up itself. Then sign in as the demo user and accept the Allow the Airline Connector to act for you screen. muse.ai should list four tools: loyalty_balance, get_loyalty_status, list_flights and book_flight (only two means an old connector: remove it and add it again). The card warns when the address is one muse.ai cannot reach, such as a local run. Prompts: a stated price ("for $620") is what the rules judge, a destination ("to London") uses the airline's price, with both your price wins; no route or date is needed.
A detection flow in front of the gateway. It flags bursts of calls and instructions hidden in tool arguments. Simulated here.

sources.title: Personal Agent Pattern (owner diagram)
sources.use: Shape of the gateway: detect, coarse, fine.

cards.label: Trigger Muse-detect
cards.description: Send seven calls in a row and watch the seventh held.

cards.label: Staff cannot pay
cards.description: Sign in as staff and try a payment. The coarse check blocks it before any amount is checked.

cards.label: Two rules can stop a booking
cards.description: Book a flight as an AI agent or as Sam directly. Your rule stops agent tickets over your limit ($500); the airline's rule stops anyone but premium members over $750 (the tier comes from the PingOne user, a missing tier is not premium). Exactly $500 and $750 pass, and both rules are listed when both fail. Use the Test controls card to switch Premier Gold and Premier Silver, or to set the agent limit ($250, $500, $1000 or your own amount), and run the booking again.

cards.label: Book a flight from muse.ai
cards.description: In muse.ai, say "Book me a flight to London for $620 tomorrow" (an AI agent cannot buy over your limit), then "Book me a flight to Denver tomorrow" (passes both rules and is within your limit, so it goes straight through), then "Book me a flight to Denver for $450 tomorrow" (booked at your price). muse.ai asks for a destination and a day first, so include them; the connector ignores the day. Real mode, owner-run.

cards.label: Connect muse.ai
cards.description: Open the Connect muse.ai card (Real, connector on). Copy the prompt into muse.ai, sign in as the demo user, check it lists four tools, then try "Book me a flight to London for $620 tomorrow", "Book me a flight to Denver tomorrow" and "Book me a flight to Denver for $450 tomorrow" (muse.ai asks for a destination and a day first, so include them). A warning shows when muse.ai cannot reach the address.

cards.label: Big payments need a person
cards.description: A payment over 500 is held until approved (simulated CIBA).
